features.description: OPTIONAL realtime layer on top of the bundled static dashboard at `DontPanic/dashboard/`. The static dashboard ships with DontPanic core (per plan 2026-05-09-003 F007) and works locally with no Firebase dependency. This adapter feature configures Firebase Hosting + Firestore as a multi-operator runtime: writes the projection into Firestore so multiple operators see live state through `onSnapshot`, configures Firebase Auth, and prepares for the Cloud Functions in F003 that handle drag-flip mutations. Firebase project target: `jarvis-a6ee1` (per plan 2026-05-03-002 D009). Single-tenant `projects/{project_id}/...` shape; multi-tenant archived per plan 2026-05-03-002 D002.
steps: Confirm `DontPanic/dashboard/` static dashboard is functioning standalone (per plan 2026-05-09-003 F007) BEFORE wiring Firebase realtime — adapter must not regress the static fallback.

Create a parallel adapter dashboard config (e.g. `DontPanic/dashboard/config-firebase.js`) that LAYERS Firestore `onSnapshot` listeners on top of the static state loader. Adapter is opt-in; static dashboard's behavior unchanged when Firebase isn't configured.
Wire `firebaseConfig` block targeting `jarvis-a6ee1` (project_id, auth_domain, storage_bucket).
Migrate listeners from `tenants/{tenantId}/...` shape to single-tenant `projects/{project_id}/...`.

Smoke test against a local fixture (Firebase emulator if available, else a static mock JSON file matching the Firestore document shape) — verify static fallback still works without the Firebase config. Real-jarvis-a6ee1 smoke test deferred to F005 per parent_acceptance_item credential gate (see plan D007).
features.acceptance: (1) `dashboard/` continues to work standalone (no Firebase config) per plan 2026-05-09-003 F007. (2) When Firebase config is provided, the dashboard adds realtime overlay layered on the static base — the static loader is still used as fallback for first paint and offline. (3) Firestore paths use `projects/{project_id}/...` (single-tenant) shape. (4) Adapter dashboard renders against a local fixture (Firebase emulator or static mock JSON matching the Firestore document shape) — full smoke test against jarvis-a6ee1 deferred to F005 per parent_acceptance_item credential gate (see plan D007).

features.description: Sync daemon — the local-side bridge that converts the projection (`dontpanic state snapshot --json` from plan 2026-05-09-003) into Firestore docs. Lives at `scripts/firebase_adapter/` — outside `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/` per D001 adapter boundary (adapter consumes the projection; never extends DontPanic core). Polls projection every 5-15s; idempotent diff-upserts. Each stream maps to `projects/{pid}/<stream>`. F002 ships the daemon code + tests against a local fixture (Firebase emulator or stubbed Firestore client); real Firestore writes to jarvis-a6ee1 deferred to F005 per parent_acceptance_item credential gate (see plan D007).
steps: Create `scripts/firebase_adapter/dontpanic_sync.py` — polling daemon.
Implement diff-based upsert: compare incoming snapshot to last-written, only write changed docs.
Add a small CLI: `python -m firebase_adapter.dontpanic_sync start [--interval 10] [--project-id <id>]`.
Tests cover the diff logic + idempotency + handling of `--include` projection responses, using a stubbed Firestore client (no real network).
Document running it as a launchd plist or systemd unit for persistent operation — operator runs this themselves once credentials reactivate.
features.acceptance: (1) Daemon module exists at `scripts/firebase_adapter/dontpanic_sync.py` with a working CLI entry point. (2) Idempotent — re-running the same snapshot against the stubbed Firestore client produces zero writes (verified by test). (3) `--include` filters honored to skip heavy streams when the dashboard doesn't need them. (4) Tests cover diff, upsert, and failure paths against the stub. (5) Real-Firestore latency measurement (≤30s end-to-end) deferred to F005 per parent_acceptance_item credential gate (see plan D007).

features.description: Cloud Functions for state-changing dashboard actions — required ONLY for the realtime adapter use case (multi-operator drag-flip / approve from a remote browser). Three callable endpoints: `kanbanMove(planId, newColumn)` → maps the dashboard's column to a plan-status flip via DontPanic MCP. `approveGate(planId, gateName)` → DontPanic MCP `approve_gate` with `confirm: true`. `triggerDispatch(planId, featureId)` → DontPanic MCP `dispatch` with `confirm: true`. Auth via Firebase Auth + DontPanic role/action matrix from USE_CASES.md (only Operator role can fire mutations from this surface; Observer reads-only). Network bridge from Cloud Function to operator-local MCP via Tailscale Funnel (recommended) / Cloudflare Tunnel / ngrok with auth — operator-side configuration documented but not enforced.
steps: Define Cloud Function signatures + auth requirements.
Implement the three callable functions using the existing Cloud Functions infra (`axiom/packages/functions/` or equivalent).
Resolve the local-MCP-from-Cloud-Function bridge — Tailscale Funnel is the recommended path; operator-side configuration documented separately.
Smoke test: call each function from the dashboard against a fixture plan, verify MCP was actually called.
features.acceptance: (1) Three Cloud Functions deployed and callable. (2) Each function calls DontPanic MCP — no direct Firestore mutation for state changes. (3) Auth required — unauthenticated calls rejected. (4) Smoke test passes end-to-end (dashboard click → Cloud Function → MCP → DontPanic state changes → sync daemon picks up → Firestore reflects → dashboard re-renders).

features.description: Firestore security rules. Read access requires authenticated operator. State-changing writes (anything in plans/gates/activity collections) DENIED for client-side calls — only Cloud Functions can write (via privileged service account). The sync daemon writes via service-account credentials too. Public/Observer-level access is intentionally NOT enabled in v0.
steps: Draft `firestore.rules` with auth-required read + service-account-only write.
Deploy rules and verify with the Firebase emulator.
Add a fixture test that asserts a client-side direct write is rejected.
features.acceptance: (1) `firestore.rules` deployed to jarvis-a6ee1. (2) Authenticated reads work; client direct writes denied. (3) Fixture test enforces the deny.
